text:
SRE Bot: Pager alert -> HIGH: 95th latency spike for tenant=biomarklabs in dedicated-vpc-us-east-1 pool. incident_id=INC-2026-0421. metrics: p95=1.8s (baseline 0.45s), error_rate=0.6% :rotating_light:

Maria R: acked. I'm on it, pulling metrics + logs. Can someone drop the recent rollout diff?

Chen L: I see an influx of long prompts from Biomark -> average seq_len ~4200 for the last 10m. KV cache miss rate up. No new model rollouts in the pool.

Kai T: Confirmed. Scheduler queue depth for that tenant jumped x6; worker backpressure increased. No OOMs. Latency increase correlates with batches hitting max_batch_tokens.

Samir P: Reproduced in staging with a replay of their traffic shape. The scheduler's current knobs: 
```
{"max_batch_tokens": 4096, "max_batch_size": 32, "queue_weight": 1.0, "dynamic_shedding": false}
```
If many long requests arrive, max_batch_tokens lets too many tokens coalesce, so tail waits for large requests.

Maria R: Proposed mitigations (temp, quick):
- flip dynamic_shedding=true for tenant (shed very long requests to reserved fallback)
- lower max_batch_tokens -> 2048 for their tenant
- bump queue_weight to 1.5 to prioritize internal fairness
- enable prefix_cache for tenant if not already

EngRuntime Bot: Current per-tenant overrides for biomarklabs: 
```
{"tenant_id":"biomarklabs","max_batch_tokens":4096,"queue_weight":1.0,"prefix_cache":false}
```

Chen L: I'll stage the override change. Plan: apply override on 1 host in the pool as canary, monitor p95 and errors for 5m, then roll to remaining hosts.

Kai T: If canary looks good, do NOT change max_batch_size yet. Lowering max_batch_tokens should reduce tail w/o harming throughput. Also add a short-lived metric alert: p95>0.8s -> rollback.

Maria R: Commands ready. Using infractl: 
```
infractl apply-tenant-override --tenant biomarklabs --set '{"max_batch_tokens":2048,"queue_weight":1.5,"prefix_cache":true,"dynamic_shedding":true}' --canary-host host-12
```

Samir P: Running canary now. host-12 config applied. Watching...

(2m later)

Samir P: Canary p95 down from 1.82s -> 0.46s. Error rate unchanged (~0.6%). No request rejections observed from shedding (thresholds not yet hit).

Maria R: Good signal. Rolling to rest of pool with 1m stagger between hosts.

(10m later)

Chen L: Rollout complete across dedicated-vpc-us-east-1 pool for biomarklabs. Current p95=0.48s, p50=0.09s. Customer impact: transient slowdown earlier, no 5xx spike, SLA breach window ~7m.

Jordan C: Noted. I'll file a post-incident ticket for follow-up: tune per-tenant quota + request-size guidance for Biomark. Recommend they shard very long sequences client-side or use streaming chunked requests.

Maria R: Handoff to Chen for follow-ups (config persisted in overrides, runbook updated). Paging escalations clear.

Chen L: Acknowledged. I'll contact account team + schedule a short remediation call with Biomark. We should also add an automatic canary rule for overrides that reduce max_batch_tokens more than 30% to require staged rollout.

SRE Bot: Incident INC-2026-0421 -> RESOLVED by oncall @Maria R, @Chen L, @Samir P. Duration 00:12:11. Follow-up: runbook/triage/doc link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-0421

Maria R: TL;DR for postmortem: spike caused by concentrated long-sequence traffic from BiomarkLabs hitting dedicated pool; mitigation = tenant override lowering max_batch_tokens + enable shedding & prefix cache; canary rollout; no data plane failures. Action items: add per-tenant request-size quotas, improve alerting for queue-depth/kv-miss, and customer guidance.
